Senses.Explanation: "Maitreya, true Maitreya, appears in billions upon billions of forms" opens a Budai verse about appearances that people fail to recognize. Later masters reuse and challenge the image in present teaching. Wanru warns that apparent recognition can stop at a shadow; Shiqi points to the many visible manifestations around the assembly. Baichi criticizes Budai's presentation, Binya recasts the line in a birthday verse, and Yushan throws down a bamboo slip to test recognition.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Maitreya, the true Maitreya, manifests in countless forms; he shows himself to people at every moment, yet people fail to recognize him.

Senses.Note: The later masters point to a fly whisk, staff, or the everyday field of things, and sometimes challenge whether recognition itself becomes another image to cling to. The verse is Budai's inherited saying; the selected Chan masters are present interpreters, not its original speakers.

Senses.Explanation: Maitreya, the true Maitreya, manifests in countless forms; he shows himself to people at every moment, yet people fail to recognize him. Budai's verse asks the assembly to recognize Maitreya in immediate, ordinary appearances. Present applications by Zixian Jue, Baichi, Shiqi, Miyun Yuanwu. The later masters point to a fly whisk, staff, or the everyday field of things, and sometimes challenge whether recognition itself becomes another image to cling to. The verse is Budai's inherited saying; the selected Chan masters are present interpreters, not its original speakers.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Walking is Chan and sitting is Chan; in speech, silence, motion, and stillness the body rests at ease
SearchAliases: walking is chan and sitting is chan; in speech, silence, motion, and stillness the body rests at ease
Senses.Note: Yongjia verse says walking and sitting are both Chan, while speech, silence, movement, and stillness remain at ease. Tianyin says this can only be spoken after sustained attention and then warns against mistaking a formula for insight. Guxue quotes the verse and asks what its at-ease substance is, rejecting borrowed gestures as an answer. Yezhu cites it to a patron and asks whether the patron has verified it directly. Zhufeng voices it at a memorial before asking how it meets the scattering of the body. Songyuan follows it with a verse refusing to assign it a price. Chushi explicitly quotes Yongjia and asks what the substance is. The wide claim is repeatedly tested in a particular moment.

Senses.Explanation: A course of conduct is the way someone actually proceeds and carries a claimed understanding. Yuanwu Keqin names the conduct of someone beyond ordinary calculation; Micang Kai contrasts conduct confined to human-and-heavenly roads with passing beyond them; and an unnamed monk asks Shoushan Xingnian where the earlier sages tread. Hongzhi Zhengjue’s compact “Samantabhadra’s conduct” and Dahui Zonggao’s warning about failing to see the conduct of the ancients confirm that the phrase names enacted precedent, not an abstract rule.

A monastery attendant is a junior or unordained worker who carries out community business. The Baizhang regulations have a hall-office attendant accompany written material to the secretary, and the Chan Grove regulations assign an attendant and laborers to carry a tray to the abbot's quarters. Dongshan Liangjie asks Wuxie Lingmo for permission to travel and is directed toward Nanquan Puyuan, while Yaoshan Weiyan asks a visitor whether traveling through the regions has found the hard-to-obtain thing. Shanhui says people travel a thousand miles to seek a lineage teacher but warns that they may still fail to take in what is offered. Zhuanyu Heng cautions that even a monastic who has left home and travels remains bound if one thing occupies his feelings. Poshan Haiming’s unnamed questioner asks what the affair of traveling on foot is, Huangbo Xiyun rebukes travelers who make themselves ridiculous, and Minister Chen Cao turns the phrase into a question for Yunmen Wenyan. These encounters test the purpose and result of real travel without making distance or visits proof of completion.

Senses.Explanation: The walking-and-understanding accord of the Chan records: the founder's test — set in the mirror-treatise, unpacked as the understanding-place being the walking-place, turned back with where-is-the-word-head, demanded of lineage heirs, and crowned in verse at the founder's own memorial. Yongming Yanshou sets the founder's stamp into the charter chapter of the Source-Mirror — bright in the buddha-mind lineament, without a hair of error, walking and understanding in accord, thereby named the ancestor — as the witness his whole transmission argument leans on, Tianran Hanshi quotes the ancients' same verdict and unpacks it in his own ruling: his understanding-place is his walking-place and his walking-place his understanding-place — not understanding so today and only walking so another day, but the ancients walked so first and only now do we understand so — against the recitation-bench monks who learn a smooth mouth and cry I know the buddha, I know the Chan way, Dufeng Shan grieves that the tricksters who merely want the thing in hand have never met the ancestor's admonition, and blames the teachers who never weigh the student's vessel yet scheme to gather disciples for private credit, dragging the school into shame, and Shenfeng Xian, asked — with one thing left Vairocana falls among ordinary men, with the myriad things gone Samantabhadra loses his sphere — how does one get to walking-and-understanding accord, turns the ask back: where is the word-head? Zhe'an Jingfan opens his ten essentials for disciples with it: the ancient learners strove hundred-citied and ten-thousand-li, hunger and cold unheeded, praise and blame unmoving, until the great matter pierced through — a walking-and-understanding-accorded one must carry the line, so fame and gain cannot fence him, while today's learners scramble for bequeathed titles and nine in ten go blank when their difference-conditions are probed, Hansong Zhicao fires the verse over monk Sanyu's pyre — one bamboo hat at ease across the whole world, walking and understanding in accord with the wondrous Lotus Flower, and after the frost-age smoke hardens, wherever he meets people the three carts are there to point to, Xueqiao Yuanxin writes the minister Li Mengbai that in this late age one truly-investigating, truly-awake person is one in ten thousand — the great master said, walking and understanding in accord, thereby named the ancestor, yet people today care nothing for it: opinion-guessing with the life-death knot intact, ten-tenths fur-and-feather resemblance, then acting wildly before others until the school gate's floor is swept, and Liao'an Qingyu at the founder's memorial holds up the incense and crowns him in verse — walking and understanding in accord, lineage-telling both penetrating, eyes emptying the four seas, breath spitting the long rainbow — not yet left the Western Heaven, deserving a good beating; once come to the Eastern Land, tolerated for now — one flower, five leaves, each taking its share of spring wind.

AlternateTargets: Conduct and insight in accord: that is what earns the name of ancestor

Senses.Note: The inherited line attributed to Bodhidharma requires conduct and understanding to accord before the name patriarch is used. Tianran explains that understanding should be where action is, and action where understanding is. Tian'an links insight with precepts, Jie'an applies it to a teacher's portrait, and Yuanjie rebukes speech without matching conduct. Yuanwu also applies the inherited line to carrying the great matter.
